title: Chaos-driven fidelity validation and safe degradation procedures
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook describes a repeatable, safe process for using controlled chaos experiments to validate fidelity-related degradation behaviors and verify that runtime fallback and degradation mechanisms preserve customer SLOs and observable correctness constraints. It codifies scenarios, observability checks, execution choreography, abort/rollback criteria, and postmortem analysis templates.

Goals

- Verify that fidelity-reduction paths (quantization fallbacks, model-variant swaps, early-stop generation, reduced-cache modes) do not violate hard SLOs or data-integrity invariants.
- Provide a safe experiment scaffold to discover unintended fidelity regressions before customer impact.
- Produce reproducible validation artifacts that can be attached to release PRs for runtime or kernel changes.

Scope and out-of-scope

- Scope: hosted and dedicated runtime clusters (services: runtime-orchestrator, kernel-scheduler, fidelity-orchestrator, kvcache-operator). Applies to text-generation and chat endpoints, model variants, and cache behavior.
- Out of scope: on-prem/private deployments that require customer approval; large-scale network partition experiments (see SRE chaos catalog).

Ownership and roles

- Experiment owner: runtime-experiments@redwood (primary: Aisha Patel).
- Oncall / safety lead: runtime-sre (pager roster).
- Observability owner: metrics-team (dashboards and PromQL queries).
- Code/infra change owner: owning sig (e.g., kernel-team, serving-runtime-team).

When to run this playbook

- Pre-release gating for: kernel scheduling changes, fallback orchestration code, quantization rollout, and model-variant routing logic.
- Post-incident hypothesis verification where fidelity changes were suspected.

Safety principles (must be followed)

1) Start in isolated sandbox environment that mirrors production traffic shape (cohort shadowing).
2) Limit blast radius: 5% production traffic max for any live experiment, with hard cap of 2% without exec-level approval.
3) Auto-abort on critical SLO breach (see Abort criteria).
4) Monitor both functional correctness (eval prompt set pass rate) and operational metrics (latency, error rate, throughput).

Signals and metrics to monitor

- SLOs (per-route):
  - request_success_rate >= 99.95% (rolling 1h)
  - p50 latency < 80ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for short-generation requests (<= 128 tokens)
  - sustained CPU/GPU utilization increase > 15% vs baseline => investigate
- Fidelity metrics:
  - eval_prompt_set_exact_match_rate (daily, cohort)
  - semantic_similarity_drop = baseline_embedding_similarity - experiment_embedding_similarity (Prometheus gauge)
  - hallucination_rate (as measured by automated evals) increase > 3 percentage points triggers abort
- Operational health: 5xx_rate, kvcache_miss_rate, kernel_queue_depth, scheduler_preempt_count

Example PromQL queries (monitoring team should add these to the experiment dashboard)

- Experiment success rate: rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",experiment="fidelity-2026-01"}[5m])
- P99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",job=~"runtime.*"}[5m])) by (le))
- KV cache miss: increase(kvcache_miss_total{shard=~"shard-.*",cohort="experiment"}[15m])

Key scenarios (examples)

1) Quantization fallback spike
- Trigger: ramp up quantized-kernel selection percentage to 50% for a shadow cohort.
- Goal: validate kernel-stability and per-token latency delta.
- Expected: p95 latency change < +20%, no increase in hallucination_rate > 2pp.

2) Model-variant early degrade
- Trigger: route a percentage of requests from gptx-3-large -> gptx-3-medium with fidelity-orchestrator policy.
- Goal: ensure rollout path preserves structured-output constraints for function-calling flows.

3) KV cache warmdown (aggressive eviction)
- Trigger: instruct kvcache-operator to clear 30% of prefix entries in selected shards; apply to a shadow cohort.
- Goal: validate degradation paths for cold-start latency and model output divergence.

Experiment choreography (step-by-step)

1) Preflight checks (must pass)
   a) Create experiment run in the experiments registry with owner, cohort definition, and hypothesis.
   b) Snapshot relevant dashboards and baseline metrics (last 72h).
   c) Ensure runbook page is linked to the release PR.
   d) Inform runtime-sre and metrics team on Slack #runtime-experiments 30 minutes before start.

2) Start in sandbox (shadow replay)
   a) Run shadow traffic with the same request surface for 60m.
   b) Validate replay fidelity by comparing rate, sequence-length distribution, and token mix.

3) Canary (limited live traffic)
   a) Open canary to 0.5% production traffic for 15 minutes.
   b) If no abort criteria are met, increment to 2% for 30 minutes.
   c) Collect automated evals against the experiment cohort (see "Automated eval harness" below).

4) Scale and observe
   a) If canary is healthy, scale to agreed maximum blast radius (<= 5%) for 2 hours, collecting full telemetry.

5) Terminate and rollback
   a) Normal termination: runbook owner marks experiment complete and attaches artifacts (dashboards, traces, evals).
   b) Abort/rollback: follow Abort and rollback procedure immediately.

Abort criteria (automatic or manual)

- Any sustained request_success_rate drop below 99.9% for 10 consecutive minutes.
- P99 latency increase > 2x baseline or absolute > 700ms for generation endpoints.
- Error budget burn rate > 3x normal baseline within 30 minutes.
- Hallucination_rate increase > 3 percentage points on eval prompt set within the cohort.
- Any data integrity violation flagged by automated checks (see Data guards).

Abort and rollback procedure (time-sensitive)

1) Safety lead runs: rctl experiments abort --id <experiment_id>
2) Runtime-orchestrator: revert routing policy: rctl routing apply --file /tmp/revert-routing-<id>.yaml
3) If kernel-level change caused the issue, trigger kernel rollback: deploy-tag rollback kernel-team <previous_release_tag> following the kernel rollback runbook.
4) Open incident in PagerDuty and tag the experiment id; collect trace dumps and attach to the incident.

Automated eval harness (what to run during the experiment)

- Use the eval-harness service to execute the canonical prompt suite (path: /integrations/evals/fidelity-suite/production-v2). The harness returns: exact_match, semantic_similarity (embedding cosine), hallucination_flags, function_call_consistency.
- Example CLI: eval-harness run --suite fidelity-suite --cohort experiment-2026-01 --out artifacts/exp-2026-01.json

Data guards and synthetic assertions

- For structured-output routes (function-calling), enforce JSON schema validation with 100% pass requirement in the canary stage. Any schema violations trigger abort.
- For safety-sensitive prompt sets, mask or exclude real customer data—use replayed anonymized traffic only.

Experiment config examples

- YAML (chaos config for quantization fallback):

  scenario: quantization-fallback-spot-check
  owner: runtime-experiments@redwood
  cohort: experiment-quant-fallback-canary
  blast_radius: 0.02  # 2%
  kernel_selector_percentage: 50
  duration: 60m
  monitoring:
    - prom_query: 'histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",cohort="experiment-quant-fallback"}[5m])) by (le))'
    - prom_query: 'increase(hallucination_count_total{cohort="experiment-quant-fallback"}[15m])'

- PromQL-based alert rule (example):

  alert: FidelityHallucinationSpike
  expr: increase(hallucination_count_total{cohort="experiment-quant-fallback"}[15m]) > 3
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity: "critical", team: "runtime-sre"}
  annotations: {summary: "Hallucination rate increased >3 in experiment cohort"}

Post-test analysis checklist

- Attach: experiment yaml, runbook link, dashboards (baseline vs experiment), eval-harness artifacts, representative traces, and kernel debug logs.
- Compute: delta in semantic_similarity (mean and 95% CI), change in exact_match rate, and all operational metric deltas.
- Decide: pass / conditional-pass / fail. Conditional-pass requires follow-up mitigation items with owners and deadlines.

Release gating and signoff

- Pass criteria: no aborts, hallucination_rate delta <= 1.5pp, P99 latency delta <= +20% absolute and within SLO, schema validation 100% for structured routes.
- Signoff: experiment owner + runtime-sre + metrics-team must approve in the experiments registry.

Known limitations and pitfalls

- Shadow replay variance: replayed traffic cannot fully reproduce upstream timing or downstream integrations, expect higher variance.
- Eval suites are necessary but not sufficient — operational telemetry complements semantic checks.
- Quantization regressions may be data-distribution dependent; run on multiple workload slices (short/long sequences).

Runbook appendices (quick commands)

- Start experiment (example):
  rctl experiments create --file experiments/quant-fallback-canary.yaml --announce "#runtime-experiments"

- Abort experiment:
  rctl experiments abort --id exp-2026-01 --reason "auto-abort: p99 latency"

- Fetch eval artifacts:
  eval-harness collect --id exp-2026-01 --dest /artifacts/exp-2026-01.json

Example dashboard widgets to include

- Top-left: p50/p95/p99 latency (route=/v1/generate) split by cohort (baseline vs experiment).
- Right: semantic_similarity distribution histogram (embedding_cosine).
- Bottom: kvcache_miss_rate and kernel_queue_depth heatmap.
